paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Real worship doesn't stay in the building. The Israelites worship in Jerusalem, and then they go out and tear down the high places, pillars and altars until every one is gone (2 Chronicles 31:1). Hezekiah then puts the priests and Levites back in their duties, and he gives from his own possessions first (2 Chronicles 31:2-3).

Then look at what the people do. Hezekiah commands a contribution so the priests and Levites can devote themselves to the Law of the LORD (2 Chronicles 31:4), and the people give generously, and they bring in an abundance (2 Chronicles 31:5). When Hezekiah asks about it, Azariah says, "…the LORD has blessed His people; this great abundance is what is left over" (2 Chronicles 31:10). I think that's the heart of it: when God's people give, God's house is taken care of, and the giving is never wasted.

The writer sums it up this way: Hezekiah "did what was good and upright and true before the LORD his God" (2 Chronicles 31:20). He "acted with all his heart in every work that he began in the service of the house of God… in order to seek his God" (2 Chronicles 31:21). So here's my question for you, baker. What's one thing you could do with ALL your heart this week, to seek God? Do that one, and leave the rest to Him.
